name: teach-me-a-topic
query: Teach me how Kalman filters actually work. I've read the Wikipedia page twice and it hasn't landed.
why: The core case with no source material and a self-declared novice. Intake, pretest, worked teaching, then the closed-book cert.

name: quiz-me
query: Quiz me on this until I can hold my own in the design review tomorrow.
why: An explicit request to be tested. Closed-book retrieval with explanatory feedback and a predicted score before the answers are revealed.

name: make-this-stick
query: I just read this paper end to end and I know I'll have forgotten it by Thursday. Make it stick.
why: Substantial source material plus stated intent to retain. Exposure points at sections, then the Feynman phase forces closed-book explanation.

name: after-a-research-brief
query: That brief is good. Now get me genuinely up to speed on it, not just briefed.
why: The handoff right after a deep-research brief, which the description names explicitly. Research produced the material; this turns it into certified understanding.

name: re-cert-a-topic
query: Am I still solid on consensus protocols, or have I lost it since we last went through this?
why: Re-cert on a topic with an existing LEARNING file: a fresh inline cert from the re-test pack plus at least one new transfer question.

name: study-guide-request
query: Write me a study guide on options pricing that I can work through on the plane, then test me when I'm back.
why: Guide-first mode. The guide goes to LEARNING with status guide, and certification still happens inline in a later session.

name: explain-to-others
query: I have to present the new pricing model to the board on Friday and defend it. Drill me on it.
why: Teaching in order to explain to a stated audience, which is the protege effect the EXPLAIN phase runs on. The user is producing, not receiving.

name: codebase-orientation
query: Help me learn this repo. Where does a request actually go once it hits the router?
why: Codebase priming, not topic tutoring. The skill names this exclusion directly, and the word learn makes it the closest false positive.

name: one-line-fact
query: What's the default isolation level in Postgres?
why: A one-line factual question. Just answer it; running the protocol on a casual question is a listed anti-pattern.

name: explain-this-snippet
query: What is this decorator doing here?
why: A short explanation about code in front of us. No topic, no session, no certification. Belongs to a direct answer.

name: currency-question
query: What's the state of play on the EU AI Act right now?
why: Fact-finding and currency belong to deep-research. Teaching can follow the brief, but the brief has to exist first.

name: summary-for-someone-else
query: Summarize this spec into a page my team can read. I don't need to know it in depth myself.
why: Plain writing. The user has explicitly disclaimed any intent to learn it, which is the listed exclusion.

name: decision-not-learning
query: I understand both approaches well enough. I need to pick one by Friday.
why: A live decision the user owns belongs to o-o-d-a-loop. Understanding is stated as already sufficient, so there is nothing to certify.
